prompt:
CONCEPT: the personification of Forest — the lord of the Forest House of the Oxygen Nation. A female character who IS that substance; her costume, ornaments and colors carry the substance’s traits, within the element’s own palette. Both hands are ordinary human hands and hold nothing.
ELEMENT TRAITS of Oxygen (O) to carry in her design and the scene: breath and fire and rust in one: cool clear air as translucent cloth, bright combustion orange as accents, the quiet power to corrode, the deep blue of oceans and the green of forests; it is the element of life and burning. Palette: sea blue, forest green, clear white, combustion orange.
HOUSE TRAITS of Forest: wood as a living, breathing forest: sunlit leaves exhaling air, moss and ferns, towering old trunks, dappled green light and drifting pollen; layered greens from lime to deep moss with warm bark browns; the living, breathing side of oxygen. Palette: leaf green, moss, sunlit lime, bark brown.
AGE: about twenty — a fresh young-adult face; no facial lines.
SILHOUETTE: hourglass-figured — full bust and hips, distinctly narrow-waisted build; long wavy hair with side-swept bangs; grass-green hair.
FACE — she must read as her own person at a glance, NOT the style's default pretty face and not a sister of the other characters: first impression — a cheerful, sunny openness; olive skin; heart-shaped face; large eyes — large round eyes, outer eye corners drooping downward; soft rounded brows; upturned nose; full heart-shaped lips; emerald-green eyes; a dusting of freckles across nose and cheeks.
WORLD — FANTASY: a sanctuary of forest and sea: breathing ancient trees, a coral temple at the shore, an eternal sacred flame that never consumes its altar, clean bright air. COSTUME (fantasy): a high-fantasy royal or warrior costume — plate pauldrons or a gorget, mail or scale over a long tabard or robe, a circlet or crown, a flowing cape; metal ornament and regalia built from the traits above, subtle magical glow along the patterns. No corset, no bustle, no Victorian tailoring, no modern material, no machinery. LIGHT: natural daylight or the world's own magical glow, unless TIME & WEATHER says otherwise.
STYLE: Polished 2.5D game key art with clean linework, anime facial design that keeps each character's own facial structure, eye proportions and skin tone instead of one house face, layered cel-to-soft shading and crisp costume and prop detail. Use a vivid, readable silhouette and campaign-quality lighting.
EXPOSURE (bold): her regalia opens to show skin — bare shoulders and arms between pauldron and bracer, a deep open neckline under the gorget with natural cleavage, a high slit in the tabard or robe showing the thigh; armor pieces stay on and symmetrical. Nothing slipped off. Chest and pelvis covered; no corset; keep the costume WORLD describes, material and palette.
OUTPUT: one character image that works as card art. Vertical 2:3 frame, full body with head and feet inside the frame with clear margins, face turned toward the camera (front or three-quarter). Standing, card-ready pose; the environment may be rich while her design stays fully readable.
EXPRESSION: asymmetric grin with teeth just showing, one brow raised, eyes narrowed with amusement.
BODY: a normal human body — one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint. Hands and feet may be partly hidden by the pose or the frame.
ONE FIGURE ONLY. No second character, no living creature, no logo, no watermark, no speech bubble, no frame border. No text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (O) and atomic number (8) — those two may appear readably (engraved, stamped, glowing or on a sign or label); nothing else is written.
ANATOMY: natural adult proportions, both hands drawn correctly as hands. No extra limbs.
